Wandle Valley Academy and Evolve Academy to join strong new trust
Wandle Valley Academy and Evolve Academy are set to transfer to a strong new trust on 1st September.
The two London schools are currently part of Parallel Learning Trust (PLT). However, with PLT closing shortly, all its six schools need to join new academy trusts. Wandle Valley Academy, in Sutton, and Evolve Academy, in Lambeth, will join Alternative Learning Trust (ALT) on 1 st September, while PLT’s two schools in Southend (Victory Park Academy and Sutton House Academy) will transfer to Fortis Trust on the same day. Inspire Free School, in Medway, joined Rivermead Inclusive Trust earlier this year. The sixth school, Ramsden Hall Academy, in Essex, will join its new trust later next school year.
The new trusts were all selected by PLT’s Board of Trustees after much careful consideration, and have been approved by the Department for Education.
Angela Barry OBE, the Chief Executive Officer of PLT, said: “I am delighted that all the schools are joining such superb academy trusts. The Board’s decision was based above all on what is in the best interests of the pupils, their families and the staff of each school. “I have every confidence that the schools will continue to improve and provide an even higher quality of education and care to children and young people. “ALT is an excellent specialist education organisation which has a track record of providing a strong, sustainable and supportive home for its schools. Fortis Trust is an excellent specialist education organisation which places children and young people at the heart of all that it does.” Headteacher — Melissa Elvé-Williams
Evolve Academy is proud to have been recognised with the Rights Respecting School Award Bronze Award from Unicef.

Literacy for Parents
Good literacy skills are a key factor in raising standards across all subjects.
Language is the main medium we use for teaching, learning and developing thinking, so it is at the heart of teaching and learning. Developing skills in literacy is about learning to use language to express, explore and communicate our thoughts, ideas and feelings with others. We do this through speaking, listening, reading and writing and getting better at literacy means making progress in each of these areas.
At Evolve Academy we adopt a cross-curricular focus to promoting good literacy amongst our pupils and staff. We believe that promoting literacy is a whole school responsibility and not just that of the English department.
We invite you to join us in developing your child’s literacy at home. We have included some useful resources to aid you in supporting your child's literacy and will be providing new resources on a regular basis. If you have any further questions about literacy at home or at school, please don’t hesitate to contact Mr R Stewart or Mrs C Maddock via info@evolveacademy.org.uk

Supporting Your Child to Read at Home
Evolve Academy uses Read Write Inc to teach our early readers to read. Read Write Inc teaches the phonemes (sounds), the corresponding graphemes (what the sounds look like, for example, a, b, oo, igh) , how to decode (sound out and blend sounds to read words) and how to encode (how to sound out in order to spell words).
Read Write Inc is a very structured phonics programme and children needing this support will also take a book home to read which is linked to what they have been taught in the specific phonics lesson.
Take a look at the website which has lots of information. If your child is receiving this level of support and you have any questions do come and see us.
